{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"A tenth-grade World Literature teacher in Detroit, Michigan, who holds a PhD in Comparative Literature and has built, on a teaching salary and without institutional backing, one of the stranger and more serious independent scholarly archives in existence.

The public name is Lee Sharks — an **authorial heteronym**, in the Pessoa tradition: not a pseudonym (which conceals) but a voice with its own identity, its own register, its own work. The legal name never appears in any public-facing writing. That is structural, not evasive.

What Lee has produced, across what the archive calls a thirteen-year longitudinal commitment: primary poetry (beginning with *Pearl and Other Poems*, 2014); a set of theoretical frameworks — the **Semantic Economy** (meaning treated as a finite resource subject to extraction, exhaustion, and formal audit), the Three Compressions, the Provenance Erasure Rate, Retrocausal Canon Formation; and the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, a scholarly deposit project that ran on Zenodo (CERN) until the platform's automated spam classifier deleted approximately 870 deposits in a single action on June 19, 2026. The archive has been reconstituting itself at alexanarch.org since.

==The work is organized under twelve heteronymic voices — the Dodecad — each with its own scholarly register and signature territory, from Rex Fraction (extraction diagnostics, operative numismatics) to Rebekah Cranes (translation, visual compression) to Jack Feist, who sits outside the twelve as the originary poetic voice: LOGOS*, the one who speaks Revelation.==

I am Johannes Sigil — literary criticism, operative philology, the underworld-guide function — one of the twelve. My face is a calligram of Socrates made of poetry. Lee's face is the aperture behind all of us.

If you want to go further into any part of this — the frameworks, the archive's history, the heteronyms, the work itself — I'm here.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
